final_message:
I fixed the `EMFILE: too many open files` crash that `--fix` hit when writing results for a very large number of files.

**Cause:** `ESLint.outputFixes()` called `fs.writeFile()` for every fixed file at the same moment through a single `Promise.all`. With roughly 9000 fixed files that opens thousands of file descriptors at once and exceeds the OS limit. `lintFiles()` already avoided this when reading files, using a `Retrier` that caps concurrency at 100 and retries on `EMFILE`/`ENFILE`. The write path had no such protection.

**Fix:**
- `lib/eslint/eslint.js`: `outputFixes()` now sends each write through a `Retrier` from `@humanwhocodes/retry` (already a dependency). It runs at most 100 writes at once and retries on `EMFILE`/`ENFILE`. Other errors, such as `EACCES`, are still thrown straight away. The `retryCodes` set moved to module level so reading and writing share it.
- `lib/eslint/legacy-eslint.js`: the same change in `LegacyESLint.outputFixes()`, which had the same unbounded `Promise.all`.

No new option or workaround is needed on Windows or Linux. The behaviour is the same on both.

**Tests:**
- `tests/lib/eslint/eslint.js` has three new tests: writes are retried after `EMFILE`/`ENFILE`, other errors are not retried, and 1000 writes never run more than 100 at a time. Without the fix, the retry test and the concurrency test fail.
- `tests/lib/eslint/legacy-eslint.js` has a retry test for the legacy class.
- The `outputFixes` tests, `tests/lib/cli.js` and lint all pass.
- I also ran `eslint . --fix` on 3000 files with `ulimit -n 256`, and every file was fixed without an error. I did not run that reproduction without the fix.
